policies.title: Kiribati citizen: right to enter
policies.summary: The official Immigration Procedures states that every Kiribati citizen has the right to enter and be in Kiribati. The same-country ordinary-passport catalog row is normalized as citizenship, not a foreign visitor visa route.
conditions: The statutory right requires proof of citizenship and identity and compliance with border requirements. It does not classify a dual national travelling on another passport or a foreign traveller’s visitor, work, transit, residence, special-document or admission case.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: visa waiver
policies.summary: The live Immigration Division page identifies the 2023 Order as current and expressly names this mapped foreign-nationality cohort among countries whose citizens may travel to Kiribati without a visa. The procedures call this mechanism a visa waiver; arrival entry processing is not normalized as a visa issued on arrival.
conditions: The current portal states a maximum 90 days in any 12-month period, a passport valid at least six months from departure, an ICAO-compliant passport, onward travel and sufficient funds.
The visa-waiver classification is limited to visitor travel. The portal directs travellers seeking work to obtain a work visa before travel.
This does not establish residence, employment, study, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document or individual admission treatment.
The portal names Greenland, Puerto Rico, Cook Islands and Niue as places but they are not independent ordinary-passport codes in this catalog; no catalog mapping is made for those place names.

conflicts.explanation: The current Immigration Division’s 2023-order schedule expressly names the United Republic of Tanzania among visa-exempt African countries; the ordinary Tanzanian-passport row is normalized as visa_free.
